title: Duchy of Spoleto
capsule: The Duchy of Spoleto was a Lombard duchy established around 570–577 CE when the Lombard commander Faroald I seized the city of Spoleto in central Italy during the broader Lombard invasion of the peninsula. It became one of the three major Lombard political units alongside the Lombard kingdom in the north and the Duchy of Benevento in the south, controlling a swath of the Apennine highlands from the Po valley foothills to the edge of Campania. Frankish conquest of the Lombard kingdom in 774 brought Spoleto under Carolingian suzerainty as a march protecting Rome from Benevento; the duchy's autonomy fluctuated under successive Frankish dukes and briefly under the Carolingian emperors themselves, who held it directly. After 888 the duchy fragmented with the collapse of Carolingian central authority, and it was progressively absorbed into the Papal States by the late 10th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory in the Umbrian Apennines is well attested in Lombard and Frankish administrative records; the fluctuating tributary zone toward Benevento and the Adriatic coast is less precisely bounded.
